}

df = pd.DataFrame(data)
df_melted = df.melt(id_vars="Year", var_name="Tax Type", value_name="Proportion of Total Revenue")

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="husl")
ax = sns.lineplot(
    legend=False,
    data=df_melted,
    x="Year",
    y="Proportion of Total Revenue",
    hue="Tax Type",
    style="Tax Type",
    markers=True,
    dashes=False,
    linewidth=2.5
)

ax.set_title("Finland Tax Revenue Trends (2000-2015)", weight='bold', size=16, pad=20)
ax.set_xlabel("Year", fontsize=12)
ax.set_ylabel("Proportion of Total Revenue", fontsize=12)
ax.legend(title="Tax Type", bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.gca().set_ylim(0.021, 0.415)
plt.savefig("output.png")
SUMMARY
 The chart titled "Estonia Tax Revenue Trends (2000-2015)" is a line graph that illustrates the proportion of total revenue contributed by different types of taxes in Estonia over a 16-year period. The x-axis represents the years from 2000 to 2015, while the y-axis shows the proportion of total revenue, ranging from 0.00 to 0.45. Five distinct tax types are plotted, each represented by a unique color and marker style: VAT Collection (red with circular markers), Excise Tobacco (gold with "x" markers), Excise Alcohol (green with square markers), Corporate Tax (teal with plus markers), and Personal Tax (blue with diamond markers).

VAT Collection consistently holds the highest proportion of total revenue throughout the period, starting at 0.32 in 2000 and gradually increasing to a peak of 0.42 in 2014 before slightly declining to 0.41 in 2015. Excise Tobacco revenue begins at 0.20 in 2000, rising to a high of 0.25 in 2007 and 2011, then gradually decreases to 0.21 by 2015. Excise Alcohol starts at 0.16 in 2000, showing a steady increase to 0.22 in 2013 and 2014, before dropping slightly to 0.21 in 2015.

Corporate Tax revenue starts at 0.06 in 2000, remaining relatively stable until a gradual increase from 2007 onward, peaking at 0.11 in 2012 and 2013, and ending at 0.10 in 2015. Personal Tax shows the smallest proportion, starting at 0.04 in 2000 and fluctuating slightly to reach a peak of 0.08 in 2011 and 2013, before declining to 0.06 in 2015. The chart effectively highlights the dominance of VAT in Estonia's tax revenue and the varying trends of other tax types over the years.
